snippet:
This is the Feishu/Lark official OpenAPI MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool designed to help users quickly connect to the Feishu/Lark platform and enable efficient collaboration between AI Agents and Feishu/Lark. The tool encapsulates Feishu/Lark Open Platform API interfaces as MCP tools, allowing AI assistants to directly call these interfaces and implement various automation scenarios such as document processing, conversation management, calendar scheduling, and more.
## Preparation
### Creating a Feishu/Lark Application
Before using the lark-mcp tool, you need to create a Feishu/Lark application:
1. Visit the [Feishu Open Platform](https://open.feishu.cn/) or [Lark Open Platform](https://open.larksuite.com/) and log in
2. Click "Console" and create a new application
3. Obtain the App ID and App Secret, which will be used for API authentication
4. Add the necessary permissions for your application based on your usage scenario
5. If you need to call APIs as a user, set the OAuth 2.0 redirect URL to http://localhost:3000/callback

Based on your usage scenario, lark-mcp supports configuring different domain environments:
**Feishu (China Version)**:
- Default uses `https://open.feishu.cn` domain
- Suitable for users in China
**Lark (International Version)**:
- Uses `https://open.larksuite.com` domain
- Suitable for overseas users or international version of Lark
To switch to the international version of Lark, add the `--domain` parameter in your configuration:
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"lark-mcp": {
"command": "npx",
"args": [
"-y",
"@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",
"mcp",
"-a",
"<your_app_id>",
"-s",
"<your_app_secret>",
"--domain",
"https://open.larksuite.com"
]
}
}
}
```

title: Advanced configuration - Lark CLI - Documentation - Lark Developer
snippet:
The MCP tool supports a wide range of command parameters, allowing flexible configuration for suitable MCP startup commands. Detailed usage instructions for each parameter are provided below in **Parameter usage examples**.

1. Run the following command in your local terminal to install lark-mcp.
```
npm install @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp -g
```

After installing lark-mcp locally, you can use the MCP tool persistently (supported command parameters are referred to in the **Command Parameters** section below). Taking [Trae](https://www.trae.com.cn/) as an example, the global installation steps are explained as follows:
- Global installation: installs to a global path (/usr/local/lib), commands are persistent, and system-level commands are available. Suitable for scenarios where command line tools are used frequently.
- NPX installation: described in the [Install and use OpenAPI MCP](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/mcp_integration/mcp_installation) document. This method allows quick installation and use, but the command is not persistent as it is installed in the system's temporary cache, deleted after execution. Suitable for quick trials or one-time usage.

2. Open the Cursor tool.
3. Open the terminal within the tool.
4. Execute the following command to log in to OpenAPI MCP as a user:
```
lark-mcp login -a <your_app_id> -s <your_app_secret>
```

### lark-mcp mcp
The supported command parameters of `lark-mcp mcp` are described in the table below.
| Parameter | Abbreviation | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--app-id` | `-a` | App ID of the Lark application. | `-a cli_xxxx` |
| `--app-secret` | `-s` | App Secret of the Lark application. | `-s xxxx` |
| `--domain` | `-d` | API domain of the Lark Open Platform, default is the Lark domain. | `-d https://open.larksuite.com` |
| `--tools` | `-t` | List of MCP tools that need to be enabled. Refer to [tools](https://github.com/larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp/tree/main/docs) and pass the corresponding **MCP tool names**. - Support passing in preset toolsets. For example, if you pass in the preset toolset for messages and groups (preset.im.default), the specified range of message and group APIs will be enabled. For details on usage, see the below **Preset tool sets** section.

| `--mode` | `-m` | Transmission mode. Optional values are: - stdio (default) - sse - streamable | `-m sse` |
| `--oauth` | None | Configurable parameter for SSE/Streamable transmission mode, enabling automatic use

title: GitHub - junyuan-qi/lark-mcp-server
snippet:
# Lark MCP Server
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server implementation for Lark/Feishu, enabling MCP-compatible applications to interact with Lark's various collaboration capabilities.
## Overview
Lark MCP Server provides a bridge between AI models and Lark's collaboration platform by implementing the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification. This server allows AI assistants to:
- Send messages to Lark users
- Retrieve calendar events
- Create new calendar events
- Add attendees to calendar events
The server uses the standard I/O (stdio) transport layer to communicate with MCP clients, making it compatible with various AI model implementations that support the MCP standard.
## Features
- **Message Sending**: AI models can send direct messages to Lark users
- **Calendar Management**:
- List events within a specific time range
- Create new calendar events with customizable details
- Add various types of attendees to events (users, groups, meeting rooms, external emails)

1. Clone the repository:
```
git clone https://github.com/junyuan-qi/lark-mcp-server.git
cd lark-mcp-server
```

### Connecting with an MCP Client
The server communicates via standard input/output (stdio). MCP clients can connect to the server by launching it as a child process and communicating through its stdin/stdout channels.

#### 2. Add the Lark MCP server configuration
Add the following configuration to the `mcpServers` section of your `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"lark-mcp-server": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["/path/to/lark-mcp-server/build/index.js"],
"env": {
"LARK_APP_ID": "your_app_id",
"LARK_APP_SECRET": "your_app_secret",
"LARK_USER_ID": "target_user_id",
"LARK_CALENDAR_ID": "target_calendar_id",
"LARK_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN": "your_user_access_token"
}
}
}
}
```
Replace the path and environment variables with your actual values. This configuration tells Claude Desktop how to launch the Lark MCP server and what environment variables to provide.
#### 3. Restart Claude Desktop
For the changes to take effect:
1. Completely quit Claude Desktop (not just close the window)
2. Start Claude Desktop again
3. Look for an icon in the UI to verify the Lark MCP server is connected
Once connected, Claude will be able to send messages to Lark users and manage calendar events on your behalf.

For more information about the Model Context Protocol, visit the [MCP Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction).

title: GitHub - phancthanhduc/lark-mcp: This is a custom Lark MCP
snippet:
# Lark MCP Server
Custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Lark/Feishu - read access to Base (Bitable), Docs, Wiki, and Sheets.
## Features
- **Base (Bitable)** - Read databases, tables, records, and views
- **Docs** - Read document content and blocks
- **Wiki** - Navigate knowledge base spaces and pages
- **Sheets** - Read spreadsheet data
## Quick Start
### 1. Install
```
cd lark-mcp-server
npm install
npm run build
```
### 2. Configure
Create a `.env` file:
```
LARK_APP_ID=your_app_id
LARK_APP_SECRET=your_app_secret
```
### 3. Run
```
# Stdio mode (for Claude Desktop)
node dist/index.js
# HTTP mode (for remote access)
node dist/index.js --http
# Server runs on http://localhost:3100
```
### 4. Connect to Claude Desktop
Add to `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"lark-mcp": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["/absolute/path/to/lark-mcp-server/build/index.js"],
"env": {
"LARK_APP_ID": "your_app_id",
"LARK_APP_SECRET": "your_app_secret"
}
}
}
}
```
## Available Tools
### Base/Bitable (8 tools)
- `bitable_get_app` - Get Base app info
- `bitable_list_tables` - List tables
- `bitable_list_records` - List records
- `bitable_get_record` - Get single record
- `bitable_batch_get_records` - Batch get records
- `bitable_search_records` - Search records
- `bitable_list_views` - List views
- `bitable_get_view` - Get view
### Documents (4 tools)
- `docs_list_documents` - List documents
- `docs_get_content` - Get text content
- `docs_get_raw_content` - Get raw JSON
- `docs_get_blocks` - Get block structure
### Wiki (3 tools)
- `wiki_get_node` - Get page info
- `wiki_list_spaces` - List wiki spaces
- `wiki_list_nodes` - List pages
### Sheets (4 tools)
- `sheet_get` - Get spreadsheet info
- `sheet_list_sheets` - List sheets
- `sheet_get_values` - Read cells
- `sheet_get_values_batch` - Read multiple ranges
### Drive (1 tool)
- `drive_list_files` - List Drive files

title: Call Lark MCP server in remote mode (Deprecated) - Lark CLI - Documentation - Lark Developer
snippet:
Lark Open Platform provides a remote MCP Server configuration feature that supports the Streamable HTTP transmission protocol, allowing users to securely and efficiently integrate and use rich Lark open capabilities in cloud scenarios with AI agents such as Cursor, Trae, Claude, and n8n via one-click integration.
## Configuring the MCP Server
Create a remote MCP service on the Lark MCP Configuration Platform and customize tools (i.e., Lark Open Platform server-side APIs) to flexibly build the MCP tools your business needs.
All tools are called via API under the identity of the currently logged-in user (user_access_token). Details:
- During the configuration process, the system guides you to complete the authorization operation for the logged-in user with one click. The MCP Server can only call tools on behalf of the user after authorization.
- The user_access_token itself has an expiry time. The remote MCP Server configuration feature supports automatic refreshing of the token before expiration.

Take Cursor as an example, to use Lark MCP services inside the AI agent.
1. Open a new chat session on the right side of the tool.
- Select **Agent** at the bottom left.
- Choose the large model as **Auto** or manually select any model (different models may have different outcomes).
2. Fill in your specific business requirements in the input box.
